content:
The “East of Eden” actor is the subject of plastic surgery speculation after some red carpet appearances.

Many internet commentators speculated about possible procedures Pugh could’ve undergone, and Pugh herself even responded to a video analyzing her face.

“Guys. I turned 30. I’m a woman. Body’s and faces change,” she wrote in the comments of the clip on Tuesday. “It’s not that deep, the fact that people can’t even tell between what’s aging and what’s surgery is disturbing. Sadly puppy fluff doesn’t last forever ❤️.”

On Pugh’s Instagram story on Wednesday, she responded to the “disturbing” comments people were making about her.

“I woke up the other morning and quite a lot of you were discussing my face and body in such a disturbing way,” she said. “I learnt online that I had been on Ozempic? I learnt that I’d had upper bleph? Lower bleph? Filler? Face lipo? Buccal fat remover? Chin surgery? Nose surgery?! What the ... hell guys, I didn’t even know that one person COULD get all of these things done over night if they wanted to? Yes I’m disturbed.”

“Here’s the truth, I turned 30 and my New Year’s resolution was to change my relationship with alcohol, and to be able to do at least one pull up in the gym,” she explained. “It’s funny to see you all use reference images from times where I was really mentally unhappy and abusing my body and put it next to the image from the Governors Awards the other night where I am happy and truly respecting my body.”

Pugh said that currently she is able “to be rested, to sleep, to wake up and work out and to eat regularly and healthily,” unlike certain other periods of her life.

“I’ve always been aware that seeing a confident woman be happy in her skin is triggering to a lot of people and for [a] long time just accepted that I will receive commentary like that,” she said. “But now this...? I’m asking us all to just be mindful. We are all real people, living real lives.”

Pugh has much more important things to focus on, as she recently threw her hat in the ring to play a Bond villain.
